cases.name: Receia Kollie
cases.about:
She was a registered nurse in the inpatient psychiatric unit at Prairie St. John’s hospital in Fargo, ND. She had been a psych nurse at Prairie since the spring of 2021, CEO Jeff Herman said, and was a beloved member of the team. “Very well respected, a great nurse. Incredibly kind person. Everything you would want from an employee,” he said.

Gabriel Barbly, pastor of Harvest Intercontinental Church in south Fargo, said Receia Kollie had been a member of the church since 2014. "She was very lively, a people person. She was a woman very determined," Barbly said. "She kept the family together."

Born in Monrovia, Liberia, Receia graduated high school in 1989, the same year the Liberian Civil War began, her family wrote on the GoFundMe website.

She fled the country with her high school sweetheart, James Kollie, and the two married, settled in the Ivory Coast on the southern coast of West Africa and started a family.

In 2001, they moved to the U.S., where Receia later pursued her dream to become a registered nurse, which she achieved at age 54.

cases.name: Jaelyn Nichole "Jae" Walker
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Jae was our beautiful, blue eyed, fearless, and feisty girl who loved singing and, although she kept it to herself, she had a beautiful voice. Her quiet time was spent in her room after making herself her macaroni and tomato juice, which was her favorite. If you had the privilege of being her friend, she would let you join too as she loved her closest friends fiercely.  

You’d never find Jae in anything but sweatpants and a sweatshirt, wrapped in one of her favorite blankets with a power fan blowing in her face. If it wasn’t comfy, she wasn’t having it. 

She loved and cared deeply for animals, especially her cats - obsessively her cats. There was no one who adored and loved her more than her big brothers and little sister, whom she loved equally as much. There was nothing Jae loved more than snuggling in bed with her mama, favorite snacks in hand, or sitting in a fishing boat for hours with her dad. 

Her favorite family time was lake time, filled with the whole family, all 40 something of us, especially her cousins. Her love of Anime gave her aspirations to travel and see the world. Jae was so proud of the choice to be baptized at Prairie Heights on May 22nd, 2022. She is now in the loving arms of Jesus. 

Words cannot ever express how much Jaelyn meant to us. We will cherish every one of her 14 years. Every single memory we have with her will last us a lifetime. She is so loved, incredibly missed, and we will carry her in our hearts forever. "
